synopsis.heading: What a percentage is
synopsis.body: A percentage is a fraction with 100 as the denominator. x% of a number means x/100 × number. Most exam questions become fast once you stop multiplying by 100 and start thinking in fractions.

synopsis.heading: Increase and decrease
synopsis.body: If a value rises by r%, the new value is (100 + r)/100 times the old one. If it falls by r%, multiply by (100 − r)/100. A 25% rise multiplies by 5/4; a 20% fall multiplies by 4/5.

synopsis.heading: Percentage change
synopsis.body: Change % = (New − Old) / Old × 100. Always divide by the original value. That is why a 20% fall followed by a 20% rise does not get you back to the start.

formulas.label: Price up r%, keep spend same

tricks.title: Swap the numbers
tricks.body: x% of y equals y% of x. Pick whichever pair is easier to compute in your head.

tricks.title: Successive change in one line
tricks.body: For two changes a% and b%, the net change is a + b + ab/100. Use a minus sign for a decrease.
